name: 96 Elite Championship
epitaph: Michael Ahriman won the Elite Championship in a three-way with Jinx and Alex Kent on 27 April 2009; Jinx held it by Screaming For Vengeance, where Requiem beat him for 'the brand new Elite Championship belt' in June, and the pages end with Requiem holding it.
notes: The June pages call it 'the WU Elite Title'; the belt is the one the April eXpose crowned Ahriman with, which is why the company is held as one under both names.

name: 96 Commonwealth Championship
epitaph: Salim Raj won the Commonwealth Championship in a three-way with Chad Vargas and Makayla Fox on 27 April 2009; Fox took it from him on 17 May and defended it against Brandon Maddox at Screaming For Vengeance and Twilight Rayn at Parental Advisory 11.
notes: The June pages call it 'the WU Commonwealth Championship'.

name: 96 Lugar Championship
epitaph: Chad Vargas was 'the new Lugar champion' on 6 May 2009; Drake Daniels beat him for it at Screaming For Vengeance on 7 June, where the commentary says the Lugar championship 'is going to become the One Shot', and Skit-Zo took the renamed belt at Parental Advisory 11.
notes: The previous holder, if any, is not named, and the June pages call the belt the One Shot title in the same breath as the old name; the name recalls the older fed's One Shot title but the lineage is this company's own.

name: 96 Revolution World Championship
epitaph: The Chaotic Cage match of 18 October 2009 crowned Johnny Styles the first '96 Revolution World Champion' (the match's own rules call it the Undisputed World Championship); Nathan Lancaster was declared champion after pinning him on 3 November.

name: 96 Prodigy Championship
epitaph: The Chaotic Cage match of 18 October 2009 gave the Prodigy title to the man pinned in the final fall: Nathan Lancaster, who defended it against Rico Sutton on 26 October and still held it on 9 November.
notes: Created by the rules of the cage match, which hand the Prodigy title to 'the man to get pinned, or submitted'; Nathan was the last man pinned.
